entries.subject: DAMIT 6205: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-6205.txt. Model 6205, version 2022-07-13, pole (36°, 30°), period 2.39006 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 1.45 ±0.2 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: No registered reusable reflectance texture was examined for the selected radar/optical model. The grid marks missing imagery; Elevation is source-model radius relative to a sphere, not measured geology.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT shape solutions
entries.finding: The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 6203: pole (210°, -30°), 2.385454 h, version 2022-07-13; 6204: pole (180°, -30°), 2.390874 h, version 2022-07-13, archive diameter 1.26 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent shape, spin or scale evidence distinguishes these alternatives, or a changed release offers a demonstrably better supported model.

entries.subject: Rożek et al. radar and optical model selection
entries.finding: Rożek et al. (2022) combines radar and optical data and reports the 1.45 ± 0.20 km prograde model 6205 as more consistent with the WISE size determination than retrograde 6204; the convex-only 6203 is not substituted. This supports retaining the selected numerical model and its calibrated scale, but it does not resolve the alternative pole, provide a registered surface map, or qualify local terrain.
